title: The Voice Comes First Now: Frame Count Follows the Words | vitalii.no
description:
Until now, the picture for each demo clip was built first and the voiceover was laid over it afterward. A 15-second clip under a 25-second narration had to loop to cover the gap, so for the second half of every video the viewer was watching something they had already seen while the voice had already moved on to new material — the eye and the ear were telling two different stories in the same clip.

The order is now reversed. The narration is written as beats, each one generated and measured separately, and the frame windows in the Remotion composition are built from those measurements instead of the other way around. FeatureInstagramPublishing was rebuilt as the reference implementation, with one figure carried through all five beats. The new audio-assembly script builds the track with ffmpeg's adelay and amix rather than a simple concat, because mp3 frames are 26 milliseconds each and a concat build came out 1.2 seconds short over five beats — enough to walk the picture off the words by the end of the clip. That drift was caught and fixed before any clip shipped with it, and the old loop-based path is now documented as legacy, kept only for the clips already made with it.

The reference clip now renders at exactly 907 frames — precisely the length of its own voiceover, not a fixed duration with a loop stitched in.
